theorem_title: Rational parameter selection for exponents above two
natural_language_statement: For every real ν > 2, there exist rational numbers θ, A, B, and C such that, when viewed as real numbers, 0 < θ < A < B < 1, ν(A − θ) > 1 − θ, 1 < C, B < 1/C, B < Cθ, and Cθ < 1.
explanation: Choose a rational b strictly between 1/ν and 1 − 1/ν, which is possible because ν > 2. Then choose a positive rational δ smaller than both 1 and (2b − 1)/b², and set θ = 1 − δ and A = 1 − bδ. These choices give 0 < θ < A < 1, the exponent-gap inequality, and A/θ < 1/A. Choose a rational C strictly between A/θ and 1/A; then choose a rational B strictly between A and min(1/C, Cθ). The interval bounds yield all required strict inequalities.
